title: Letting the ritual begin in time

captions.physics: Returning to a familiar shared pleasure
captions.energy: Delaying desire for a suitable moment

meaning: A familiar ritual can delight you more freely when waiting for suitable conditions does not turn participation into an account of unfulfilled promises.
text: A familiar pleasure can remain a promise longer than either wishes. The Hierophant in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes an accepted form of leisure: returning to a small ritual and performing familiar actions. The Hanged Man in energy leans towards postponing desire for a more suitable moment or another perspective on conditions. Justice in emotions allows fairness of participation to be felt. A pause can be considerate, yet prolonged waiting invites comparison between who has prepared and who postponed again. Pleasure then risks becoming duty instead of a free beginning.

For example, you agree to prepare occasional small surprises for an evening together. One person has chosen an amusing postcard, while the meeting waits again for complete readiness. **Familiar pleasure needs a free and understandable agreement between you.** You can choose a simple version for today without requiring surprises of equal scale. The ritual keeps its pleasant purpose: delighting and meeting, beyond an unnamed quota of effort and waiting.

The difficulty is restoring fairness by counting every postponement. You promise better preparation, delay again and gradually make a small pleasure too weighty. Honesty demands compensation while desire loses its voice. A pause helps when it reveals a suitable way to participate. A modest evening can fulfil your intention better than an impeccably prepared meeting that still has no place.
